notes: SEED / DRAFT — hand-authored on 2026-09-17 to create the repository with real content.
This file is the LISTING: one row per template repository we keep, website and app alike.
It is NOT the machine source of truth for resolution. A template is usable because its
repository exists and carries its own metadata; the platform discovers templates by scanning
catalogOrganization for repositories whose name ends in 'template' and reads each one's
.works/template.yml and .works/works.yml. This file adds curation (pin, license class,
managed-hosting decision, verification) and makes a template listed, badgeable and searchable.
Rows with status 'placeholder' name repositories that do not exist yet (created by APW-13).

`template.ref` is a branch for a website row (the existing fork-from-branch behaviour) and for an app row while it is a placeholder; on publication an app row's `template.ref` becomes the release tag `v<blueprint.version>` and `template.sha` its commit (CI check 3 in README.md §2).

templates.name: Umami
templates.summary: Privacy-first, cookieless web analytics: one container, one Postgres, heartbeat health check.
notes: Metadata-only: the template holds the App spec and nothing else. The app source stays in
umami-software/umami, so provisioning forks TWO repositories (the app source first, the template
second). The App Work's Work Repository is the app-source fork.
The shipped spec deploys the upstream's published image pinned by digest; switching build.strategy
to dockerfile builds the fork, which is why the app-source fork must exist (blueprint README §Evolving).
Created by APW-13 T27 (seed content: APW-13-golden-paths/blueprints/umami/).

templates.name: App fixture (hello)
templates.summary: The acceptance fixture: the smallest app that makes every App spec feature observable.

managedHosting.reason: Test fixture; it is exercised by the acceptance lanes and is not offered for hosting.

notes: TWO DIFFERENT REPOSITORIES — do not conflate them (the plan does today; see plan-changes.md §5):
ever-works/app-fixture-hello          = the fixture APPLICATION (source only, no .works/), and it is a
GitHub *template repository* so the estate helper can generate
per-run upstreams from it. It is NOT an App Blueprint repository.
ever-works/app-fixture-hello-template = the App BLUEPRINT repository (the App spec).
'template repository' in the GitHub sentence above means the repository setting, not a Blueprint.
Created by APW-13 T22 (application) and T24 (Blueprint).
Listed because it is referred to by a template row above, not because it is a template:
its name does not end in 'template', so the suffix scan never returns it
(isStandardTemplateRepository in packages/agent/src/template-catalog/template-catalog.service.ts:1047-1049).
Acceptance lanes never fork it directly — they generate throwaway upstreams from it in the test
organization so every run gets a fresh fork network (APW-13 plan §2.2, ACCEPTANCE §0.3).
